rule.title: Cross-chain proof verification insufficient — forged import payload can trigger arbitrary transfers

intent.attack_thesis: The contract implements a cross-chain bridge import/relay surface (submitImports, proveImports, processTransactions, executeMessage, relay, or similar) that accepts an externally-supplied proof payload (Merkle proof, transaction proof, receipt proof, state proof). If the verification of that proof is insufficient — the root is caller-supplied, the proof parser has no domain-binding, or the follow-up execution trusts proven data without re-checking token/amount bounds — an attacker can forge a payload that passes verification and triggers arbitrary asset transfers out of the bridge contract.

preconditions: proof verification does not bind to a trusted on-chain root (or root is manipulable)
execution phase trusts verified payload fields without independent checks
steps: attacker crafts a PartialTransactionProof / receipt proof with fabricated transfer(s)
attacker calls submitImports / relay / executeMessage with the forged proof
bridge verification routine (proveImports / verifyProof) passes the payload
bridge execution routine (processTransactions / executeMessage) executes contained transfers
escrowed tokens are transferred to the attacker's drainer wallet

reporting.title_template: Bridge import surface `{function}` accepts caller-supplied proof without sufficient verification — potential cross-chain proof forgery
reporting.summary: Matches bridge contracts with publicly-callable import/relay/execute surfaces that consume bytes/struct proof arguments. Fires when: (1) the proof verification root is caller-supplied or stored in mutable storage without trusted-relayer/validator-set guards, AND (2) the execution phase performs asset_transfer or delegatecall using data derived from the proven payload.
reporting.user_summary: This bridge contract accepts cross-chain proofs from any caller. If the proof verification is insufficient, an attacker can forge a proof to drain escrowed funds.
reporting.technical_summary: The detector identifies contracts with bridge-pattern selectors (submit*, prove*, relay*, execute*, process*) that accept bytes/struct calldata arguments consumed by hash/verify paths. It checks whether the Merkle/proof root is derived from a trusted on-chain source (anchor, validator set, L1 state root via precompile) or from caller-supplied data. When the root is untrusted and the post-verification path reaches asset_transfer effects, the finding fires.
reporting.exploit_narrative: An attacker constructs a PartialTransactionProof containing fabricated transfer instructions. The proof is structured to pass the bridge's verification routine (either because the root itself is caller-controlled, or the proof parser has insufficient domain-binding). Upon successful verification, the bridge's execution layer processes the contained transfers, sending escrowed tokens to the attacker's wallet.

preconditions: bridge import/relay surface is externally callable
steps: identify the proof structure expected by the verification function
craft a minimal proof payload that passes verification
include a transfer instruction targeting the attacker wallet
call the import/relay surface with the forged proof
verify token transfer from bridge to attacker
